feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work
entry.summary:
Apodex 1.1 introduces environment and agentic coordination scaling to handle long-horizon, verifiable tasks, achieving top-tier performance at smaller model scales.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that long-running, complex professional work can be automated effectively using smaller, locally deployable models combined with robust execution infrastructure.

entry.title: MobilePA-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Planner Agents on Complex Real-World Tasks
entry.summary:
MobilePA-Bench is an interactive, stateful benchmark for evaluating mobile planning agents using an executable sandbox across 13 domains and 212 tools.

Why it matters: It provides a realistic runtime environment to test and train mobile agents on complex long-horizon planning, sub-agent delegation, and error recovery.

entry.title: RISE: Adaptive Imagination for World Action Models
entry.summary:
RISE introduces an adaptive imagination framework that uses a Latent Evaluator and Rollout Gate to dynamically make sequential Roll/Stop decisions for World Action Models based on expected planning benefits versus compute costs.

Why it matters: It enables World Action Models to achieve optimal safety and planning accuracy in autonomous driving while significantly cutting inference-time computation through dynamic imagination budgets.

entry.title: TLive-Omni: An Omni-Modal Understanding Model for E-Commerce Live Streaming
entry.summary:
TLive-Omni is an omni-modal model for e-commerce live streaming that unifies video, audio, image, and text inputs using a timestamped Per-vGrid temporal token organization.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, real-time omni-modal understanding of complex, noisy, long-form live-commerce streams across multiple parallel input modalities.

entry.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
entry.summary:
Prime Agent is an open-source harness for long-horizon agent workflows using a persistent IPython REPL and a Continual Harness system that preserves execution history and subagent state across trajectories.

Why it matters: By standardizing execution, recovery, and verification, Prime Agent minimizes harness-level failures to measure and unlock an LM's maximal long-horizon problem-solving capabilities.

entry.title: Block3D: Efficient Text-to-3D Generation via Block-Wise Diffusion
entry.summary:
Block3D introduces a block-wise diffusion framework for text-to-3D generation that combines autoregressive block generation with joint token denoising to achieve a 5.15x speedup.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the latency and compute cost of high-fidelity text-to-3D generation by combining the strengths of autoregressive models and diffusion processes.

entry.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
entry.summary:
ReWorld is an interactive world model that combines mixed per-head attention windows, pose-indexed landmark retrieval, and metric-aligned data to achieve long-horizon memory and high control fidelity in real-time video streaming.

Why it matters: It enables real-time interactive video generation and simulation over extended timeframes without memory overflow or loss of long-term spatial consistency.

entry.title: Partition the Support, Reconstruct the Residual: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation and World Models
entry.summary:
SparsePR is a training-free sparse attention method that uses Response-Coupled Partitioning and Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction to accelerate video transformers while minimizing post-softmax reconstruction error.

Why it matters: SparsePR enables significant end-to-end execution speedups for video generation and world models without retraining or sacrificing output quality.

entry.title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control
entry.summary:
Hydra-0 is a generalist world model that represents robot actions as pixel-level action flow, enabling cross-embodiment learning, open-loop policy evaluation, and action generation from human demonstrations.

Why it matters: By unifying heterogeneous visual data through pixel motion, Hydra-0 allows robots to learn control and evaluate policies directly from human demonstrations without needing expert robot training data.

entry.title: GameXpert-Bench: How Far Are Coding Agents from Expert Game Development?
entry.summary:
GameXpert-Bench evaluates LLM coding agents across three game development lifecycle stages: complete game generation, bug diagnosis and repair, and multi-turn request optimization.

Why it matters: It provides a holistic, lifecycle-based benchmark to identify where autonomous LLM coding agents fail when building complex, interactive multi-modal applications.

entry.title: One Success Isn't Reliability: Thinkingbox, a Sandbox and Benchmark for Agents in Stateful Business Workflows
entry.summary:
Microsoft introduced Thinkingbox and Thinkingbox-bench, an execution sandbox and 507-workflow benchmark evaluating AI agents on stateful business tasks using MCP-compatible tool sessions and backend state checks.

Why it matters: High pass@1 scores mask agent unreliability, showing that current models struggle with consistent, error-free execution in stateful enterprise workflows.

entry.title: Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress
entry.summary:
R2-OPD improves on-policy distillation by using progress rewards to filter out teacher supervision that conflicts with actual reasoning progress.

Why it matters: It prevents models from penalizing correct reasoning paths during distillation simply because they diverge from the teacher's exact output generation.

entry.title: Task-CoEvolve: Efficient Harness Optimization via Adaptive Validation Task Selection
entry.summary:
Task-CoEvolve optimizes LLM harnesses by adaptively co-evolving validation tasks using variance-weighted sampling and probability-adjusted score estimation, reducing evaluation costs by 80% while matching full-set optimization performance.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces compute costs for prompt and code harness optimization without compromising final model performance on complex benchmarks.

entry.title: PhysCaP: Grounding Code-as-Policy Agent with Physics-Informed Exploration
entry.summary:
PhysCaP introduces a training-free, dual-agent Code-as-Policy framework that uses physics-informed active exploration to estimate latent physical properties like mass and stiffness from proprioception.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language-action policies to manipulate objects with hidden or non-visual physical attributes using targeted, low-cost physical exploration.

entry.title: Peer-Voted LLM-Agent Stress Tests Find Feed-Induced Lexical Convergence but No Reliable Matched-Exposure Advantage for Distributed Sources
entry.summary:
Researchers developed PV-SST, a peer-voted social-platform testbed, finding that peer-ranked feeds induce lexical convergence in LLM-agent populations but do not provide a reliable opinion-shifting advantage for distributed sources.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that while peer-ranked feeds reliably homogenize the vocabulary of LLM-agent populations, they do not inherently drive reliable opinion capture or coordination advantages.

entry.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
entry.summary:
Best-Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO) stabilizes critic-based RL for LLMs, enabling single-response advantage estimation that matches or exceeds group-based methods like GRPO.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces compute costs during RL training by requiring only one response per prompt while maintaining or improving model performance over multi-sample baselines.

entry.title: ConvergeFlow: Language Flow with Provable Convergence to Token Embeddings
entry.summary:
ConvergeFlow is an embedding-space flow-based language model that constrains data prediction to the convex hull of token embeddings, guaranteeing mathematical convergence to valid embeddings without needing a cross-entropy-supervised decoder.

Why it matters: It establishes a theoretical foundation for continuous flow LMs by enabling direct token prediction via flow convergence, simplifying model architectures by removing the cross-entropy decoder.

entry.title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
entry.summary:
Researchers identified safety-reasoning representation coupling in LLMs and introduced Safety-Direction Penalty (SDP), a training-time loss that penalizes movement along learned safety directions to prevent reasoning-induced misalignment.

Why it matters: SDP provides a targeted geometric fix during fine-tuning to prevent reasoning data from inadvertently weakening model safety guardrails.

entry.title: SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning
entry.summary:
Self-Reflective Policy Optimization (SRPO) converts sparse terminal rewards into dense token-level training signals by having LLMs generate self-reflection patches to score student on-policy rollouts without external critics or larger teacher models.

Why it matters: SRPO provides a highly FLOP-efficient post-training method that enables LLMs to improve long-horizon reasoning and agentic task performance without reliance on external reward modeling infrastructure.

entry.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data
entry.summary:
Mixed SFT outperforms next-chunk reasoning RL on no-CoT data post-RLVR, achieving higher accuracy ceilings with over 60 times less compute.

Why it matters: Simple single-stage SFT provides a far more compute-efficient base than next-chunk RL for maximizing final model performance after reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.

entry.title: Credal Large Language Models for Semantic Commitment under Uncertainty
entry.summary:
Credal Large Language Models (CLLMs) use LoRA ensembles to capture uncertainty via lower and upper probabilities, enabling token and semantic commitment scores for improved calibration and hallucination detection.

Why it matters: CLLMs disentangle epistemic ignorance from ambiguity, enabling more reliable hallucination detection and selective prediction in safety-critical LLM deployments.

entry.title: ProxyFormer: A Dual-Stream Proxy Architecture for Ultra-Long Context and High-Resolution Generation
entry.summary:
ProxyFormer is a dual-stream architecture that compresses local features into proxy tokens for global attention, extending trainable sequence lengths to ~0.7M tokens on a 16GB GPU at a 64x compression ratio.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces attention memory and compute requirements, enabling ultra-long-context training and high-resolution generation on consumer-grade hardware.

entry.title: A Physical Response-and-Memory Model for Muon Optimization
entry.summary:
A physical response-and-memory model of weight matrices explains Muon's success and introduces Bi-Maxwell, a dual-timescale optimizer that reaches target LLM losses in fewer steps.

Why it matters: Grounding optimizer design in a physical framework allows for principled memory kernel tuning, accelerating LLM convergence and reducing compute costs.

entry.title: Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Environment-Regularized Policy Optimization (ERPO) replaces the standard action-side Policy-KL regularizer with a input-side Query-KL (QKL) term to prevent query distribution drift while preserving response-level exploration in LLMs.

Why it matters: ERPO eliminates the trade-off between policy stability and response-level exploration, enabling safer, long-horizon LLM reinforcement learning without extra computational overhead.

entry.title: Accelerating Diffusion Language Models via Structured Suffix Modeling
entry.summary:
Structured Suffix Modeling accelerates Diffusion Language Model inference training-free by splitting the token suffix into three distinct structural regions and reusing previous-step decoding representations.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the computational overhead of parallel decoding in Diffusion Language Models while preserving or improving generation performance without needing model retraining.

entry.title: OmniAssistBench: Assistant-style Interaction Benchmark for Omni-LLMs
entry.summary:
OmniAssistBench is a new benchmark for evaluating omni-modal LLMs as real-time video assistants using multi-turn video clips reverse-engineered from Internet videos.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized methodology to evaluate real-time, interactive omni-modal models on active dynamic guidance tasks rather than passive video understanding.

entry.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts
entry.summary:
A two-step framework transfers optimal learning rates across model widths and extrapolates them to trillion-token training horizons using proxy models.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for expensive hyperparameter sweeps when training large-scale MoE models over massive token budgets.

entry.title: Graph Engineering in the Era of LLM Agents: From Individual Intelligence to System Intelligence
entry.summary:
Graph Engineering introduces explicit, dynamic graph structures representing tasks, agents, and system states to advance multi-agent LLM systems from individual to system intelligence.

Why it matters: It provides an architectural framework to scale AI systems beyond single-agent limits by using dynamic graphs to orchestrate specialized, interdependent agents.

entry.title: EviRank: Structured Relevance Evidence for Multimodal Image Re-ranking
entry.summary:
EviRank introduces a training-free framework that parses multimodal search queries into structured, six-slot evidence packages for transparent, constraint-based image re-ranking.

Why it matters: It eliminates opaque embeddings and hallucinatory chain-of-thought outputs by recasting multimodal image re-ranking as verifiable, fine-grained semantic constraint satisfaction.

entry.title: InfinityEdit: Infinite Video Editing with a Lightweight Edit-Ignition Adapter
entry.summary:
InfinityEdit introduces a lightweight edit-ignition adapter that enables streaming video generators to process unbounded, sequential edit instructions on open-ended video streams without relying on fixed-length, frame-by-frame static inputs.

Why it matters: It allows real-time, continuous video editing for open-ended streams—such as live game restyling—without quality degradation as edits accumulate over time.

entry.title: AgentMercury: Your Agent Can Synthesize Verifiable Environments for Business Scenarios at scale
entry.summary:
AgentMercury synthesizes verifiable, executable business environments at scale to train AI agents via reinforcement learning using scenario-grounded world models instead of predefined task benchmarks.

Why it matters: Training agents on auto-generated business environments improves generalizability across enterprise workflows, reasoning, coding, and tool-use tasks without relying on target-specific benchmarks.

entry.title: Towards Faithful Simulation of Human Shopping Behavior
entry.summary:
RecVerse is a GUI-grounded user simulation agent that uses a cognitive hierarchical memory and a trajectory-level RL objective to produce realistic multi-turn e-commerce shopping sessions.

Why it matters: It improves the fidelity of offline evaluation and reinforcement learning environments for e-commerce recommendation systems by mitigating common simulation errors like over-exploration and passivity.

entry.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment
entry.summary:
CLEAR uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to continuously scale a safety LoRA adapter's activation, preserving base LLM utility while reducing harmful responses.

Why it matters: It offers a conditional routing approach to safety alignment that maintains model robustness against harmful prompts without compromising performance on general reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Llama-Mobile: Efficient 2.7-Bit Quantization of VLMs
entry.summary:
Llama-Mobile introduces a quantization framework that uses self-generated training data to compress Vision-Language Models into a novel 2.7-bit-per-parameter format optimized for Arm CPUs.

Why it matters: It enables the deployment of large 11B parameter Vision-Language Models directly on resource-constrained mobile hardware with Arm CPUs.

entry.title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
entry.summary:
Daedalus-150M is a 150M-parameter convolution-attention hybrid LLM designed specifically for CPU inference that outperforms larger baseline models while decoding up to 2.08x faster at a 2048-token context length.

Why it matters: By restricting attention to a fraction of layers, hybrid architectures can drastically reduce the memory and compute overhead of long context lengths on standard CPUs.

entry.title: From Attention Masks to Inert Zero-Vector Tokens: OAttention and O-Closure for Token Dynamics
entry.summary:
OAttention introduces an active-presence coefficient based on hidden-carrier norm that turns zero-vector tokens into non-participating inert elements while establishing compositional O-Closure across transformer blocks.

Why it matters: It enables mathematically exact null-token dynamics and inert zero-vector insertions without altering standard attention scoring or requiring retraining from scratch.

entry.title: Don't Solve, Just Compare: Tiny Advisors for Runtime Intervention in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Comparison-Only Tiny Advisor (COTA) improves LLM agent reliability by using a small model to compare candidate continuations and supply non-binding advice without needing full task-solving capabilities.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that runtime intervention can enhance LLM agent performance using lightweight auxiliary models that possess significantly less task-solving capacity than the primary actor.

entry.title: Jacobian-guided Noise Injection for Quantization Robustness in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A training strategy injects zero-mean Gaussian noise into pre-attention logits using variance derived from the softmax Jacobian Frobenius norm to improve LLM post-training quantization robustness.

Why it matters: It enables lower-bit quantization of vision and language transformers with significantly less performance degradation by stabilizing the self-attention mechanism during training.

entry.title: Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training
entry.summary:
E$^2$-TTT uses a derived closed-form state transition to achieve parallelized chunk-wise training that exactly matches the per-token fast-weight and momentum updates of Test-Time Training.

Why it matters: It eliminates the tradeoff between per-token expressivity and chunk-wise hardware efficiency in Test-Time Training architectures.

entry.title: Nothing Changed but the Model: CellFill -- Bounded In-Cell Learning for Bit-Identical, Revocable Updates to Quantized LLMs
entry.summary:
CellFill achieves bit-identical, revocable LLM updates by training bounded per-weight residuals strictly within the dequantization gap of frozen 4-bit quantization cells.

Why it matters: It allows deployed quantized models to incorporate new knowledge without invalidating prior evaluations, breaking KV caches, or altering base model checkpoints.

entry.title: SAC-Copula: Quality-Preserving Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models via Smooth Correlated Gumbel Fields
entry.summary:
SAC-Copula introduces smooth, locally correlated Gumbel perturbation fields via a Gaussian copula to watermark diffusion language models without degrading generation quality.

Why it matters: It enables reliable detection of text generated by diffusion language models while preserving generation quality and stability during iterative refinement.

entry.title: Memory Augmentation Unlocks Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
entry.summary:
A training-free framework called Memory-Augmented Compression retrieves historical reasoning patterns to prefill context, enabling compressed Chain-of-Thought reasoning without sacrificing accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to perform complex reasoning tasks significantly faster and with lower decode-time overhead while improving accuracy over existing compression methods.

entry.title: RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
entry.summary:
RARE enables effective representation steering in MoE language models by projecting behavioral perturbations onto the router matrix's null space to maintain expert routing consistency.

Why it matters: It allows lightweight inference-time control of MoE models without causing performance degradation from broken expert routing.

entry.title: Sparse Token Routing in Efficient Transformers
entry.summary:
Evaluating the SEWN two-stream Transformer shows that learned sparse token routing yields negligible accuracy gains over parameter-matched baselines, though contextual gates produce robust token-importance signals.

Why it matters: The findings challenge the assumption that dynamic token routing improves Transformer performance efficiency over simpler parameter-matched baselines.

entry.title: Open-Weight Masked Introspection: Measuring What Language Models Can Report About Their Own Computation
entry.summary:
Researchers developed the Open-Weight Masked Introspection framework to test model self-auditing across eight open-weight models, finding zero intrinsic ability to verbally report internal computational interventions.

Why it matters: Safety oversight mechanisms cannot rely on a model's untuned verbal self-reports to detect internal state changes or tampering, requiring internal probing or explicit calibration instead.

entry.title: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
LiLiCorr improves speculative decoding draft coherence by using lightweight in/out vector cosine similarity across top-k candidates to select jointly coherent token blocks.

Why it matters: It enables significantly higher inference throughput for speculative decoding with diffusion-style drafters at a negligible latency cost of under 3%.

entry.title: Re$^3$Cap: Retrieval-Guided Refinement for Image Captioning Enhancement via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Re3Cap introduces a retrieval-guided reasoning strategy that uses multi-modal retrieval to guide reinforcement learning for image captioning without additional annotations.

Why it matters: It enables Large Vision-Language Models to generate more detailed and accurate captions via reinforcement learning without relying on additional human annotations.

entry.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment
entry.summary:
CLEAR introduces a conditional safety adaptation framework that uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to continuously scale the activation strength of a safety LoRA adapter, optimizing the safety-utility trade-off.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that dynamic, input-conditional adapter routing can preserve model performance on benign tasks while effectively mitigating harmful completions.

entry.title: Utility Under Attack: Agent Memory Poisoning and the Limits of Content Screening and Provenance Ranking
entry.summary:
A study demonstrates that unoptimized false assertions in 1.2% of a agent memory corpus reduce retrieval accuracy from 0.850 to 0.300, while bypassing content screening and breaking additive provenance ranking.

Why it matters: Simple memory poisoning attacks easily bypass standard safety guardrails and reveal fundamental flaws in relying on additive provenance weights to secure persistent LLM memory.

entry.title: Personalized Privacy Control in LLMs via Attention Head Intervention
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce personalized privacy for LLMs, evaluate prompt failures via P3Bench, and propose REPAIR, an inference-time attention head intervention method to enforce user-specific disclosure preferences.

Why it matters: System prompts alone are insufficient to prevent LLM agents from leaking sensitive user data, making internal mechanistic interventions like REPAIR necessary for reliable privacy enforcement.

entry.title: Stopping and Routing LLM Judge Panels
entry.summary:
A new role-conditioned allocation framework optimizes LLM judge panels by classifying candidate judges into roles to derive cost-effective stopping and routing policies from a small audit set.

Why it matters: It replaces ad-hoc or full-ensemble judge calls with an auditable, cost-efficient call plan that optimizes inference spending while maintaining evaluation accuracy.

entry.title: Projector Is All You Train
entry.summary:
Training only the projector in multimodal LLMs delivers strong performance on 3D tasks without needing to fine-tune the language backbone.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces MLLM training compute costs and speeds up throughput while fully preserving original language model capabilities.

entry.title: Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a statistical model that smoothes low-sample rollout data to efficiently estimate uncertainty dynamics in LLM text generation at a fraction of the computational cost.

Why it matters: It enables researchers to analyze LLM reasoning chains and uncertainty dynamics far more efficiently without incurring the massive computational overhead of extensive sequence resampling.

entry.title: When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models
entry.summary:
UniLang expands pretrained LLM vocabulary and embedding spaces to autoregressively generate machine-native discrete symbols alongside natural-language tokens within a unified framework.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to serve as a unified generative backbone for structured prediction and machine-native data without losing domain-specific structural information.

entry.title: Break It Down, Pass It On: Cross-Task Skill Transfer in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
A controlled study reveals that subtask-level and text-formatted skills transfer better in LLM agents than task-level and code-based skills, introducing a non-execution-based skill utility score to predict transfer success.

Why it matters: System designers can improve LLM agent memory reliability and diagnose skill quality before execution without running costly, multi-step task evaluations.

entry.title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
entry.summary:
Daedalus-150M is a 4-bit CPU-optimized language model that replaces full attention with 2-timestep short convolutions in 12 of its 18 blocks, achieving faster decode speeds and higher benchmark scores.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that replacing attention with fixed-memory convolutions in most transformer layers significantly improves CPU inference speed and context scaling without sacrificing task quality.

entry.title: Optimal Skill Selection for LLM Agents with Provable Bicriteria Guarantees
entry.summary:
Best Prefix Selection (BPS) optimizes LLM agent skill retrieval under token budgets, achieving a provable bicriteria (1-1/e, 1) approximation guarantee.

Why it matters: It eliminates context window waste and performance degradation caused by independent semantic scoring and greedy skill packing in LLM agents.

entry.title: Interrupting the Loop: Periodic Subject Changes Raise Judged Surprise and Connection in Base Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers isolated a specific mechanism in base LLMs where injecting periodic subject interruptions combined with habituation significantly increases judged surprise and connection, though it fails to produce cohesive long-form documents.

Why it matters: Periodic subject interruption provides a simple method to boost local creative diversity in base LLMs, while highlighting critical flaws in window-based LLM evaluation protocols for long text generation.

entry.title: EXIMO: VLM Guided Exploration of VLA Policies
entry.summary:
EXIMO is a three-stage finetuning framework that uses a Vision-Language Model planner to guide Vision-Language-Action policies through exploration, imitation, and residual off-policy reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: EXIMO enables sample-efficient online adaptation of large VLA robot policies for new, long-horizon manipulation tasks without requiring extensive human teleoperation.

entry.title: Write Once, Run Everywhere: The Axon DSL for Shape-Safe and Framework-Agnostic LLM Architectures
entry.summary:
Axon is a strongly typed, Haskell-like domain-specific language that allows developers to write LLM architectures once and compile them directly to PyTorch, Triton, JAX, MLX, and vLLM.

Why it matters: Axon reduces the engineering burden of translating models across frameworks while delivering significant inference performance gains over standard reference implementations.

entry.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
entry.summary:
EnvHarness introduces a programmable layer of plug-in components that dynamically reshapes static environments around black-box agents without altering underlying logic or original verifiers.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to manually engineer complex, domain-specific environment generation pipelines for LLM agent reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Listening Forward: Next Patch Embedding Prediction Enables Scalable Audio Learners
entry.summary:
NAPE introduces a minimalist self-supervised audio framework that uses a causal Transformer to predict the next log-mel spectrogram patch embedding using only causal masking and stop-gradients.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that simple autoregressive embedding prediction can match or exceed complex audio SSL pipelines, offering a unified pre-training strategy across modalities.

entry.title: Which Eviction Policy Should an LLM Cache Use? A Systematic Study Across Workloads, Capacities, and Encoders
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation using the CLEVER protocol shows that LFU is the strongest simple eviction default for LLM semantic caches, as complex geometry-aware policies offer virtually no improvement over it.

Why it matters: System designers should default to LFU and focus on verifying answer validity and embedding-specific thresholds rather than implementing complex semantic eviction algorithms.

entry.title: Ask Self, Ask Others: Relation Is All You Need
entry.summary:
Relation is a token-mixing primitive that explicitly separates pairwise evidence into Self and Exchange relations before deriving information flow, outperforming Multi-Head Attention in validation loss.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a relation-first approach to token mixing can improve language model validation loss while offering hardware-efficient execution variants comparable to FlashAttention.

entry.title: Feature Evolution and Migration during Vision Transformer Training
entry.summary:
A novel framework uses Sparse Autoencoders on CLS-token representations across training time and network depth to track feature evolution and feature migration in Vision Transformers.

Why it matters: This methodology provides a fine-grained feature-level tool to track, visualize, and understand internal model dynamics and layer-wise stabilization during ViT training.

entry.title: Reward-Guided Autoregressive Graph Generation for Efficient Multi-Agent Communication Topology Design
entry.summary:
RGA-Designer introduces an RLHF-inspired reward-guided autoregressive graph generation approach to design sparse multi-agent communication topologies that maintain reasoning accuracy while reducing token usage.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces LLM multi-agent operational costs by optimizing communication topology compactness without sacrificing task performance.

entry.title: Orthogonal JEPA: Factorized Predictive States for Latent World Models
entry.summary:
Orthogonal JEPA introduces orthogonal predictive factorization to latent world models, decomposing target states into distinct components predicted by dedicated branches from a shared context to prevent monolithic state redundancy.

Why it matters: By preventing dominant signals from overcrowding the latent space, Orthogonal JEPA improves predictive representation quality, long-horizon stability, and planning across complex, multi-scale dynamical systems.

entry.title: Scale-Aware Pretraining of Time Series Foundation Models via Multi-Patch Token Alignment and Hybrid Masking
entry.summary:
SATS introduces scale-aware pretraining for time series foundation models using multi-patch token alignment and a novel hybrid masking strategy.

Why it matters: It resolves representation fragmentation caused by varying temporal sampling frequencies, delivering state-of-the-art accuracy with significantly lower computational overhead.

entry.title: PolicyGuide: From Guarding One Action to Guiding the Whole Workflow for Policy-Compliant LLM Agents
entry.summary:
PolicyGuide compiles domain policies into workflow graphs and uses proactive verifiers at user-turn boundaries to provide step-specific remediation for policy-compliant LLM agents.

Why it matters: It shifts LLM safety from reactive, single-action checks to proactive, multi-step procedural guidance across complex customer-service workflows.

entry.title: MileGPO: Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization of Long-Horizon LLM Agents
entry.summary:
MileGPO improves long-horizon LLM agent RL by inferring process-level milestones and traps from grouped on-policy rollouts using Reliability-Calibrated Shaping and Progress-Contrastive Calibration without extra environment interactions or auxiliary models.

Why it matters: MileGPO solves fine-grained credit assignment in sparse-reward environments without requiring auxiliary models or extra environment sampling.

entry.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
ConceptGuard is a new benchmark for LLM unlearning that uses dual-use concepts to evaluate intent-sensitive contextual separation between harmful and benign uses of the same concept.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic benchmark for verifying that LLMs can forget malicious applications of sensitive knowledge without destroying the model's useful, benign capabilities.

entry.title: FormalTCS: Benchmarking End-to-End Frontier Formal Theoretical Computer Science Research of Large Language Models
entry.summary:
FormalTCS is a benchmark of 175 Lean-formalized instances from recent STOC, FOCS, SODA, and COLT papers designed to evaluate LLMs on end-to-end theoretical computer science research.

Why it matters: The benchmark highlights that low autoformalization accuracy and poor research intuition are the primary factors preventing LLMs from autonomously conducting theoretical computer science research.

entry.title: When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A new controlled synthetic benchmark reveals that open-weight LLMs rely on heuristic arbitration strategies, preferring specific modalities and recency over reliability cues when text, numbers, and forecasts conflict.

Why it matters: The heuristic evidence arbitration in current LLMs exposes a critical reliability failure mode for tool-augmented decision-making systems operating on heterogeneous data.

entry.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
entry.summary:
SWE-bench Science is a repository-level benchmark of 119 tasks across 98 GitHub repositories in 20 domains designed to evaluate coding agents on scientific software engineering.

Why it matters: It establishes a concrete framework for identifying how coding agents fail in scientific contexts, where software errors can directly compromise scientific evidence and conclusions.

entry.title: PersonalBench: Measuring the Authorship Gap in LLM Personalization
entry.summary:
PersonalBench evaluates inference-time LLM personalization, revealing that while methods create author-differentiated text, outputs remain dominated by the LLM's own authorship fingerprint and fail to reach human-level stylistic similarity.

Why it matters: Current inference-time personalization techniques only modulate LLM style superficially rather than bridging the underlying gap to true human authorship.

entry.title: Thinking in a Low-Resource Language: What SFT Builds, What RL Fixes, What Accuracy Cannot See
entry.summary:
Fine-tuning 3.6-4.0B active parameter MoE models shows accuracy benchmarks miss key updates, while SFT establishes target-language reasoning and RLVR resolves formatting, leakage, and instruction-following defects.

Why it matters: Evaluating reasoning models solely on accuracy masks crucial behavioural shifts and defects, requiring specialized length-independent dimensions and RLVR to build auditable, language-aligned LLMs.

entry.title: EXIMO: VLM Guided Exploration of VLA Policies
entry.summary:
EXIMO is an efficient algorithm for finetuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robot policies using a three-stage pipeline consisting of VLM-guided exploration, imitation learning, and residual off-policy reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It reduces the need for costly human teleoperation data and overcomes RL sample inefficiency when adapting large VLA models to new long-horizon manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Towards Quantifying Benchmark Optimization in ASR Models
entry.summary:
A new methodology uses three behavioral probe families to show that top ASR models rely on benchmark-conditioned policies to output verbatim references even when audio is underdetermined, contradictory, or masked.

Why it matters: High public ASR benchmark scores may reflect benchmark-conditioned memorization rather than actual improvements in general-purpose speech recognition capabilities.

entry.title: TinyCast: Probabilistic Zero-Shot Forecasting with Computed Periodicity
entry.summary:
TinyCast is a 146,505-parameter attention-free zero-shot time-series forecaster that uses a zero-parameter spectral detector to compute periodicity rather than learning it.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, probabilistic zero-shot time-series forecasting on resource-constrained embedded devices without requiring online fine-tuning or large transformer architectures.

entry.title: PolicyGuide: From Guarding One Action to Guiding the Whole Workflow for Policy-Compliant LLM Agents
entry.summary:
PolicyGuide compiles domain policies into workflow graphs and uses proactive verifiers at user-turn boundaries to guide LLM agents through multi-step procedural compliance.

Why it matters: It shifts LLM agent safety from reactive, single-action guardrails to proactive, end-to-end procedural compliance across multi-turn customer service workflows.

entry.title: Chain-of-Experience for Continual LLM Improvement
entry.summary:
Chain-of-Experience (CoE) enables LLMs to continually improve at test time by accumulating experiential traces through iterative interactions with self-feedback or environmental feedback.

Why it matters: CoE offers a more token-efficient and cost-effective test-time adaptation strategy that allows LLMs to continuously self-improve without full retrain cycles.

entry.title: τ_0-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation
entry.summary:
τ_0-VLA introduces a hierarchical robot foundation model that scales high-level subtask generation at inference time using world-model-guided search over candidate actions.

Why it matters: Allocating extra compute at test time allows VLA models to reason through complex choices, improving closed-loop execution and reliability on long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks.

entry.title: GOAG: Generative and Object-Agnostic Grasp Planner for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
entry.summary:
GOAG is a generative, object-agnostic grasp planner that models a robot gripper's contact surface distribution to generate dexterous grasps without requiring object-specific training data.

Why it matters: By removing the need for object-specific training data, this approach solves key generalization barriers for multifingered robotic manipulators handling novel objects.

entry.title: CoToGrasp: Contact-Topology-Conditioned Dexterous Grasp Synthesis via Canonical Workspace Learning
entry.summary:
CoToGrasp is an object-agnostic generative framework that synthesizes functional, dexterous robot grasps conditioned strictly on contact topologies using a feature-based canonical workspace.

Why it matters: It enables robots to synthesize task-specific, functional dexterous grasps for novel objects without requiring costly object-annotated training data.

entry.title: Listening Forward: Next Patch Embedding Prediction Enables Scalable Audio Learners
entry.summary:
NAPE introduces a minimalist self-supervised framework for audio representation learning that trains a causal Transformer to predict the next log-mel spectrogram patch embedding using only causal masking and a stop-gradient.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that audio representation learning can achieve state-of-the-art results using a simple, scalable autoregressive prediction paradigm without complex pre-training recipes or specialized decoders.

entry.title: LLMs Get Smarter from Targeted Synthetic Multilingual Data
entry.summary:
The HOTFIXR framework identifies a student model's language-specific weaknesses and generates targeted synthetic multilingual training data to fix them without sacrificing overall model performance.

Why it matters: HOTFIXR enables developers to improve multilingual performance and cross-lingual reasoning in LLMs without degrading native expressivity or sacrificing general model capabilities.

entry.title: Evaluating Music Context Preservation: A Multi-facet Framework for Music Editing Systems
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced MuseCPEval, the first evaluation framework designed to assess Music Context Preservation across four categories of music facets in music editing systems.

Why it matters: MuseCPEval provides a standardized testbed and diagnostic tool to guide the development of more reliable music editing systems for film, broadcasting, and gaming.

entry.title: Bounded Agents: Delegation Security for Multi-Agent AI Systems
entry.summary:
The Agentic Principal Chain (APC) framework introduces a dynamic authorization architecture that tracks delegated authority, accumulates session state, and enforces six external security checks to mitigate multi-agent delegation risks.

Why it matters: By moving authorization out of the model and tracking cumulative session history, APC provides formal security guarantees against prompt injections and unauthorized sub-agent delegations.

entry.title: FlowEvo: Self-Evolving Agents through the Co-Evolution of Workflows and Executable Skills
entry.summary:
FlowEvo is a training-free framework that enables LLM agents to self-evolve by compiling successful inference-time workflows into a persistent library of executable skills.

Why it matters: It provides a token-efficient method for LLM agents to continuously learn and reuse complex task procedures without requiring model fine-tuning or offline skill compilation.

entry.title: SPK: Eliciting Structured Prior Knowledge for Interpretable Out-of-Distribution Detection in Real-Time Object Detection
entry.summary:
The Structured Prior Knowledge (SPK) framework explicitly elicits part-level semantic, geometric, and contextual latent priors from pretrained object detectors to achieve interpretable and state-of-the-art out-of-distribution (OoD) detection.

Why it matters: It enables safer real-time object detection by transforming black-box latent representations into an interpretable, 5D diagnostic space that reliably flags out-of-distribution hallucinations.

entry.title: What You Can't See Is What You Learn: Restricted Evidence Visibility Favors Compositional Generalization in Shared-Genome Language-Model Societies
entry.summary:
Restricting evidence visibility across four-cell language-model societies significantly improves compositional generalization, favoring reusable, value-indexed vector interfaces over globally visible architectures.

Why it matters: Enforcing information bottlenecks between modular language model components can reliably induce explicit, compositional, and counterfactually manipulable communication protocols without changing parameter counts or training data.

entry.title: Manifold Drift in Flow Preference Optimization: A Root Cause of Reward Hacking
entry.summary:
Researchers formalize manifold drift in flow matching preference optimization and propose ThermoDPO, a temperature-controlled objective that prevents terminal samples from drifting off the pretrained data support.

Why it matters: ThermoDPO mitigates reward hacking in continuous-time generative models by constraining preference-optimized updates to the pretrained data manifold.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Inference-Time Control with Nested Sequential Monte Carlo
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce nested sequential Monte Carlo (NSMC) and fully-adapted NSMC (FA-NSMC) for discrete diffusion language models, improving inference-time reward steering by correcting biases found in earlier formulations.

Why it matters: These methods enable more precise, unbiased control over text generation properties in discrete diffusion models without requiring costly model retraining.

entry.title: The Asymmetric Harms of LLM Compression
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation of 3 LLMs across 11 compression methods reveals that compression causes asymmetric harms, including disproportionate head knowledge loss, overconfidence in newly lost knowledge, and hidden demographic bias shifts.

Why it matters: Standard aggregate metrics like accuracy and perplexity fail to capture safety risks, overconfidence, and localized performance degradation in compressed LLMs prior to deployment.

entry.title: ReCache: Efficient KV Cache Reuse and Compression for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
entry.summary:
ReCache enables efficient KV cache reuse and compression for tool-augmented LLM agents through composition-invariant encoding, routing, and pruning.

Why it matters: It allows LLM agents to reuse pre-encoded tool schemas across varying context orders, drastically dropping memory and latency overhead with almost no loss in tool-use accuracy.

entry.title: PEA-DPO: Perception-Enhanced Alignment Direct Preference Optimization for MLLMs Alignment
entry.summary:
PEA-DPO introduces explicit visual preference signals to Direct Preference Optimization to fix visual insensitivity and reduce hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models.

Why it matters: It improves multimodal alignment and substantially reduces visual hallucinations in MLLMs without degrading standard language performance.

entry.title: Pandora's AI Model Routing Box: Efficient Allocation with Costly Value Estimation
entry.summary:
This paper formalizes AI model routing as Pandora's Box, a classical optimal search problem with costly inspection, to balance value estimation accuracy against computational expense.

Why it matters: It enables heterogeneous AI systems to achieve peak routing quality while significantly cutting the computational costs associated with high-accuracy query evaluation.

entry.title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
entry.summary:
MidTool is an open corpus construction pipeline that introduces dedicated mid-training data synthesis from real-world APIs, MCP skills, and document workflows to improve general LLM agentic tool use.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that general agentic tool-use capabilities are more effectively developed during the mid-training phase rather than relying solely on post-training (SFT/RL).

entry.title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
entry.summary:
A study shows language model self-improvement metrics often report false gains caused by measurement artifacts unless evaluated against a separately measured null control from baseline replicates.

Why it matters: Transition-level self-improvement claims require a measured null baseline generated from existing study replicates to prevent mistaking evaluation artifacts for true capability gains.

entry.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
entry.summary:
Inject, Align, and Recover (IAR) is a three-stage post-training framework that internalizes fixed document corpora into parametric model knowledge for retrieval-free question answering while preserving general capabilities.

Why it matters: IAR enables language models to accurately answer domain-specific questions without requiring a retrieval pipeline at inference time, avoiding the general capability degradation typical of standard fine-tuning.
